feedback: If a learner drops the empty hundreds column or misplaces digits (342, 3,42, or 30,042), return to the columns and show that removing the zero slides the 3 down into the hundreds place (342), while an extra zero pushes it up into the ten-thousands place (30,042); either way its value changes. The zero holds the hundreds place open.

If the expanded form or line placement contradicts the numeral just written (e.g. writing 3,000 + 400 + 2 for 3,042), translate explicitly: point to the 0 in 3,042 and ask what term it contributes (none — that is why there is no hundreds term).

Probe with: 'Why is there no "+ something hundred" in the expanded form?', 'If I take the zero out and write 342, what happened to the 3?', and 'How did you decide where on the line to put it — what did you find first?'
activities.intendedInsight: Position determines value: the zero in the hundreds column is a placeholder that must be kept, and the numeral, expanded form, and line position must all agree because they describe one number.
learnerActions: Read place-value counters such as 3 thousands, 0 hundreds, 4 tens, 2 ones and write the numeral (3,042).
Write the same number in expanded form (3,000 + 40 + 2) and explain why there is no hundreds term.
Show roughly where 3,042 sits on a 0-10,000 line — a little above the 3,000 mark, just under a third of the way along.
Translate in the reverse directions too: given a marked point, name the number; given expanded form, build the counters.
Explore what changes if a column changes: e.g. 3 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens, 2 ones gives 3,402 — and discuss how moving the counts between columns shifts the number's value and its line position.
activities.title: Three-view translation with a placeholder zero
